profile.summary: CellPLM is a pre-trained transformer for single-cell transcriptomics that treats each cell as a token and a tissue (a set of cells) as a sentence, so it can model relations between cells. It takes gene expression for a set of cells and outputs cell embeddings; the repository's tutorials apply it to cell embedding, cell type annotation and spatial imputation.

summary_quotes.text: we propose a new pre-trained model CellPLM , which takes cells as tokens and tissues as sentences
we leverage spatially-resolved transcriptomic data in pre-training to facilitate learning cell-cell relationships

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Instead of treating genes as tokens, CellPLM treats cells as tokens and tissues as sentences. It is pre-trained on single-cell and spatially resolved transcriptomic data so that it learns cell-cell relations, and it uses a Gaussian mixture prior on the latent space as an extra inductive bias. The shipped configuration names a flowformer encoder (4 layers, hidden size 1024), a gmvae latent module with 512 dimensions and 16 clusters, and a decoder module named nbmlp, trained with masking of 75% of nodes and 25% of features.

quotes.text: which takes cells as tokens and tissues as sentences
introduce a Gaussian mixture prior distribution as an additional inductive bias to overcome data limitation

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Checkpoints are on Dropbox and the authors say they may update them. The README names 20230926_85M as the latest version (dated 10/10/2023); the repository ships a config file of that name whose internal name field reads 20230926_75M_50M; the cell embedding tutorial loads 20231027_85M. The sources do not explain these differences. A result should name the checkpoint prefix exactly and the repository commit.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Single-cell pre-trained language model that encodes cell-cell relations (cells as tokens).

quotes.text: is the first single-***Cell*** ***P***re-trained ***L***anguage ***M***odel that encodes cell-cell relations
takes cells as tokens and tissues as sentences

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer encoder (config: flowformer, 4 layers, hidden size 1024), Gaussian mixture latent (gmvae, 512 dimensions, 16 clusters) and a decoder module named nbmlp; the config's architecture field is OmicsFormer.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: An AnnData object of single-cell expression; the checkpoint config lists its genes as Ensembl IDs (out_dim 19374). Spatial transcriptomic data were used in pre-training.

quotes.text: we leverage spatially-resolved transcriptomic data in pre-training

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Cell embeddings (a tensor returned by pipeline.predict). The repository has annotation and imputation tutorials, which were not read.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: Not stated as a figure. The checkpoint names carry 85M (20230926_85M, 20231027_85M), but no source gives a parameter count.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Not given in the sources read beyond the abstract's statement that single-cell and spatially resolved transcriptomic data were used. The config records dataset_num 484 and batch_num 12596, without explanation.

quotes.text: we leverage spatially-resolved transcriptomic data in pre-training

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: 20230926_85M (named latest in the README) and 20231027_85M (loaded in the tutorial). The README points to a Dropbox folder for checkpoints.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: Not stated. Cells are the tokens; the config sets max_batch_size 4000, which the sources do not describe as a context limit.

facts.label: Weights licence
facts.value: Not stated. The checkpoints are in a Dropbox folder with no licence file among the sources read.

run_guide.summary: Install CellPLM, download a checkpoint from Dropbox and compute cell embeddings for an AnnData file with the embedding pipeline from the tutorial.
prerequisites: Python 3.9 and CUDA 11.7 or later are recommended by the README.
A GPU build of PyTorch 1.13.0 or later installed first.
A checkpoint downloaded from the Dropbox folder into a local ckpt directory.

steps.title: Get the code and environment
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/OmicsML/CellPLM
cd CellPLM
git checkout --detach b59ee7688b1bd2a745856a610248b46f15019a22
conda create -n cellplm python=3.9 -y && conda activate cellplm
conda install cudatoolkit=11.7 -c pytorch -c nvidia
pip install -r requirements.txt
steps.explanation: The README's full installation; the clone and checkout lines are added by Rewire to pin the reviewed commit.

quotes.text: conda create -n cellplm python=3.9 -y && conda activate cellplm

steps.title: Download a checkpoint
steps.shell: # Download the checkpoint files from https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fo/i5rmxgtqzg7iykt2e9uqm/h?rlkey=o8hi0xads9ol07o48jdityzv1&dl=0 into ./ckpt
steps.explanation: The README gives only a Dropbox link. The tutorial expects the files in a ckpt directory.

steps.title: Embed cells
steps.shell:
python - <<'EOF'
import anndata as ad
from CellPLM.utils import set_seed
from CellPLM.pipeline.cell_embedding import CellEmbeddingPipeline

PRETRAIN_VERSION = '20231027_85M'
DEVICE = 'cuda:1'
set_seed(42)

data = ad.read_h5ad('../data/gse155468.h5ad')
data.obs_names_make_unique()
pipeline = CellEmbeddingPipeline(pretrain_prefix=PRETRAIN_VERSION, # Specify the pretrain checkpoint to load
                                 pretrain_directory='../ckpt')
embedding = pipeline.predict(data, # An AnnData object
                device=DEVICE) # Specify a gpu or cpu for model inference
EOF
steps.explanation: Lines from the tutorial notebook, wrapped in a shell heredoc by Rewire. Adjust the data path, ckpt directory, checkpoint prefix and device to your setup.

outputs: A tensor of cell embeddings, which the tutorial stores in data.obsm['emb'] for neighbours and UMAP.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The tutorial's data file ../data/gse155468.h5ad is not shipped with the commands shown; its source is GEO GSE155468.
The checkpoint prefix in the tutorial differs from the README's latest version.
